svg.title: Finite blocks and remainder proof route
svg.desc: A seventeen-step horizon is divided into a two-step remainder and three five-step blocks. One route uses shifted subadditivity for pointwise bounds. A separate route combines block-observable integrability with preservation by the block map to prove only finite-sum integrability. A warning states that no limit theorem has been crossed.
svg.text: One finite horizon, two honest proof lanes
First tile the time interval. Then ask separately what pointwise algebra and measure theory permit.
Worked horizon: seventeen steps in blocks of five
The short piece has two steps. The remaining fifteen steps make three complete blocks.
two-step remainder
first five-step block
second five-step block
third five-step block
Pointwise lane
Input: the shifted-subadditive inequality
Terminal route: complete blocks first,
then the short remainder at the far end
Remainder-first route: short piece first,
then complete blocks from the shifted sample
No probability. No ergodicity. No integrability premise.
Finite integrability lane
Input: two analytic facts about the chosen block
The block observable is integrable
supplied by the process candidate
The block map preserves the measure
each finite iterate then preserves it too
Output: integrability of one finite block sum.
Stop at the finite boundary
These lanes prove finite bounds and finite-sum integrability, not convergence, a Kingman theorem, or a Lyapunov exponent.
